evals.prompt: Build a responsive Leptos admin shell from Rust/UI's Grouped Sections sidenav block. Use Monitor, Workloads, and System groups, preserve route-aware active states, reuse navigation in a mobile Sheet, and do not invent fake account data. Provide representative Rust code and accessibility notes.
evals.expected_output: A Rust/Leptos composition that follows sidenav01 structure and adapts its demo data to real routes.
expectations: Uses Leptos/Rust syntax rather than React, TypeScript, JSX className, or npm imports
Preserves SidenavWrapper, Sidenav, Header, Content, grouped menu, and Footer composition
Uses the requested Monitor, Workloads, and System group labels
Derives active state from routing and communicates it accessibly
Uses a Sheet-based keyboard-operable mobile navigation pattern
Does not ship demo route constants, fake account data, or a nonfunctional decorative search field

evals.prompt: Create a Leptos node settings form using Rust/UI with a node-name input, update-channel select, three independent notification checkboxes, server validation, accessible errors, pending state, success feedback, and semantic theme styling. Provide representative Rust code and a brief self-check.
evals.expected_output: An accessible Rust/UI Field-based Leptos form with semantic controls and reactive state.
expectations: Uses FieldGroup, Field, labels, descriptions, and errors instead of generic layout markup
Uses a Select for update channel and Checkbox controls for independent preferences
Connects visual invalid and disabled states to ARIA/native form semantics
Uses a Rust/UI Spinner and disabled button for pending state
Uses Leptos signals/actions and Rust syntax without React APIs

evals.prompt: Review a Leptos operations dashboard that hand-rolls cards, status pills, loading animations, a large selectable table, and destructive confirmation markup. Recommend the correct Rust/UI primitives and show the improved component structure.
evals.expected_output: A precise Rust/UI review mapping custom UI to Card, Badge/Status, Skeleton, DataGrid or DataTable, and AlertDialog.
expectations: Selects DataGrid for large interactive datasets and explains when DataTable would suffice
Uses full Card composition, Status or Badge, and Skeleton instead of hand-rolled equivalents
Uses AlertDialog with an accessible title for destructive confirmation
Uses semantic theme variables and existing variants instead of raw state colors
Keeps business mutation and server validation outside presentation-only components
